uncited: Hybrid and Parallel Rendering encompasses techniques that combine splatting with other rendering paradigms (such as ray casting or mesh rendering) or distribute the splatting workload across multiple processors to achieve performance and visual fidelity improvements.
The Hybrid and Parallel Rendering family shares the fundamental mechanism of enhancing the basic splatting pipeline through hybridization or parallelization.
Hybrid and parallel splatting techniques emerged to address the scalability and visual fidelity limitations of early volume rendering methods.
As volume datasets grew larger and hardware capabilities expanded, researchers sought ways to leverage parallel processing and hybrid rendering pipelines.
